sentences.text: CodeSOTA presents itself at three of its own addresses as three things: its homepage is titled "CodeSOTA — One Routing Layer for AI Tasks", its dispatch on Papers with Code calls it "the v2 replacement for what PWC did", and its about page calls it "an independent registry of machine-learning benchmarks"; the MMRS record gives the first two, a routing layer for AI tasks on the homepage and a successor to Papers with Code on the /papers-with-code/ pages, by Kacper Wikiel for Fabryka AI in Warsaw, and does not cite the about page.

The MMRS record observes "two faces at two addresses": the homepage presents the routing product and names Papers with Code only in a footer link, which reads "Papers with Code Story", while the pages under /papers-with-code/ present the succession; the Capture Registry (2026-10-29) finds the same on re-reading the homepage and reads it as two compositions by the entity itself, the homepage composing a routing product and its Papers with Code pages a successor.

The dispatch joins the faces in its own words: "the registry is routable", every benchmark row an API endpoint, and the "router" it is slowly building would send a prompt or a document to the current state of the art without the caller rewriting code.

sentences.sense: what it is: a routing layer for AI tasks
sentences.text: On the homepage the router compares models for documents, code, speech and vision, lets a user inspect benchmark evidence and offers "the CodeSOTA selection and execution API": start from the work, compare on quality and cost, inspect the evidence and choose a route through a common API; the footer says CodeSOTA "helps developers choose AI tools for documents, speech, and coding", which the MMRS record carries as its self-description, and the record gives its unit as an AI task routed to a model chosen by benchmark evidence, quality and cost.

sentences.sense: what is available and what is planned
sentences.text: What exists and what is planned are stated apart (homepage): "Available today: model selection across the registry and an execution API for code & text. Document, speech, and vision execution are planned."; the preview "returns model recommendations. It does not process your files or run inference."; speech routes are "future" and the coding API "existing"; the direction is "a common API and account across AI tasks, with versioned recipes and a stable output contract for each task", and the roadmap brings provider adapters, versioned recipes, task validation, fallback and usage accounting into the same layer.

Each task keeps its own output format across providers; documents are the next execution family, scans and PDFs turned into text, tables or fields; speech is transcription and voice generation compared on language coverage, latency, intelligibility and deployment; coding is generating functions or repairing a repository (homepage); the dispatch's FAQ has CodeSOTA building comprehensive benchmarks "starting with OCR and document AI" and rebuilding task pages, dataset cards and method explanations "gradually, in the open, one modality at a time".

sentences.sense: evidence: benchmark observations and the Pareto frontier
sentences.text: The route is chosen on evidence (homepage): a user compares "actual benchmark observations" and inspects the Pareto frontier, where every dot is a recorded result and a highlighted model has no competitor in its cohort at least as good on both axes and strictly better on one, with quality, latency and cost measured "as coverage grows".

Its pages state the evidence's limits: "A strong result on one test does not guarantee a fit for your documents, recordings, or repository" and reported results are to be told from independently reproduced runs (homepage); third-party numbers are listed for coverage and not claimed as reproduced, "reproduced" means "an independently executed run or a signed container hash — not an aggregated claim", and "What never publishes is a number with no source" (dispatch); the registry "is a record of results; the primary literature is still the primary literature", every row linking to the source that is cited (about page).

sentences.sense: what it is: a registry of benchmarks
sentences.text: On its about page CodeSOTA is "an open, dated record of machine-learning benchmarks", maintained by one person with paid vendor work kept apart from ranking integrity, and its commitment is "a registry, not a leaderboard": a leaderboard is a view of "who is on top right now", a registry "the record that makes that view legible".

The about page's unit is the benchmark row, "a task-dataset-metric triple with a declared direction, a fixed split, a reproducibility package and a dated submission", each row with a verification tier (self-reported, community-reproduced or Codesota-reproduced) and each score dated; the MMRS record's unit is the routed AI task, and the two stand each with its source.
The MMRS record enters it as a database in the role of discovery, its lifecycle active as observed on 2026-10-28.

sentences.sense: the record kept apart from the entity
sentences.text: The MMRS record keeps itself apart from the entity it describes: "each page has two nodes, the MMRS record and the entity it describes", each assertion with a source and a basis, the lifecycle kept apart from the observation that saw it.

sentences.sense: the record's rules: code, dates, corrections
sentences.text: The dispatch claims five qualities of Papers with Code "at its best, carried forward into Codesota by default rather than by aspiration": every submission carries code, and "If it does not run, the row does not publish"; every score carries its publication and verification dates; and the about page adds that a wrong score's correction stays visible: "Nothing is silently deleted."

It refuses the class in which the MMRS meta-aggregator's census enters it: "Unlike aggregator sites, CodeSOTA verifies results independently" (dispatch, FAQ), and it is "Not a press-release aggregator", a score becoming a row only with "a reproduction path and a dated submission" (about page); the MMRS record counts it in the census as its clearest case of a successor claim made in the name's own address space.

sentences.sense: the successor to Papers with Code
sentences.text: The dispatch, dated 25 July 2025 in its metadata and issued 22 April 2026, is "our record of what happened, what was lost, and where to look now — with Codesota positioned as the calmer, stricter successor", its successor "traceable, dated, routable", and it directs users to CodeSOTA "for maintained SOTA leaderboards, benchmark pages, API replacement notes, and links to the frozen paperswithcode-data archive".

sentences.sense: the successor to Papers with Code
sentences.text: The about page dates the start to 10 December 2025, "after Meta retired Papers with Code", a launch "as an explicit successor attempt" to rebuild the infrastructure "in a way that cannot be retired by a press release"; the dispatch says CodeSOTA is "rebuilding this infrastructure independently", which the MMRS record quotes, and the record types the relation as claims_succession_to Papers with Code.

The shutdown record of 7 May 2026 does not name a single heir: "There is no single drop-in replacement. Pick by job", the archive for history and CodeSOTA for live SOTA; the dispatch holds that none of the successors Meta pointed at, Hugging Face Trending Papers, Semantic Scholar and Connected Papers, replicate "the unified paper-code-benchmark-dataset-method linkage", and its "v2 replacement" and the shutdown record's "no single drop-in replacement" stand each on its page.

sentences.sense: Papers with Code as it records it: what it was
sentences.text: Papers with Code was, in the dispatch, "in effect, the Wikipedia of machine-learning research", papers linked to implementations and benchmarks organised as Task, Dataset, Metric tuples with leaderboards, acquired by Meta (then Facebook AI) in December 2019 from Robert Stojnic and Ross Taylor under a commitment to "remain a neutral, open and free resource", its 9,327 leaderboards, 79,817 paper-to-code linkages and 5,628 datasets no longer served; the MMRS record of Papers with Code takes those figures from CodeSOTA, and the record of CodeSOTA notes that they are the dead aggregator's, its own catalogue counts not given and left unchecked.

sentences.sense: Papers with Code as it records it: the end
sentences.text: Meta retired Papers with Code in July 2025, "without prior notice" on 24–25 July (dispatch; shutdown record, "observed around July 24-25"); the domain now redirects to Hugging Face Trending Papers and "the leaderboards are gone", users "pushed toward Hugging Face" while the task-based tracker and public API went unmaintained; the MMRS record of Papers with Code cites CodeSOTA, with hyper.ai, for the redirect to Hugging Face.

sentences.sense: where Papers with Code's data went
sentences.text: The data, in the dispatch, was rescued as JSON dumps on GitHub, the pwc-archive on Hugging Face and 2021-era imports into the Open Research Knowledge Graph, "The data survives; the integrated experience does not"; the dumps serve "reconstruction, citation checks, and migration work" and are not a current leaderboard (shutdown record); CodeSOTA hosts historical PWC data as a frozen JSON dump at /browse/pwc (dispatch; MMRS record), and whether its own scores derive from the dumps the MMRS record leaves unchecked.

Its data are an open JSON registry and /api/sota, "Programmatic current-SOTA lookup for agents and internal tools" (MMRS record; shutdown record), published under CC BY 4.0 with the JSON at /data/benchmarks.json the canonical form (about page), "Built in public from Warsaw · open JSON · rankings stay earned" (homepage).

The homepage's header reads "By Fabryka AI" and its colophon "Built by Kacper Wikiel in Warsaw"; the about page has it "written and maintained by Kacper Wikiel", one public codebase, one editor, submissions going through a reproduction run and not a panel, "Self-directed · not venture-backed", with "no investors, no board, no growth targets"; the MMRS record gives the operator as "Kacper Wikiel, 'By Fabryka AI' (Warsaw)", and its "for Fabryka AI" and the about page's "Self-directed" stand each with its source.

It is "Maintained independently, not owned by any single model vendor", sponsored evaluations flagged (dispatch), and vendors may pay for custom benchmarks, commissioned evaluations, profile pages and publication support, disclosed inline, "The public ranking method is not for sale" (about page).

The MMRS records keep the name's claimants apart: CodeSOTA "carries the name in its own paths and presents itself as a successor", Papers with Code is "NOT CodeSOTA, which uses the name in its paths", and "The original's frozen dumps, CodeSOTA's succession claim and this revival are three entities around one name", the revival at paperswithcode.co "a third claimant to the name"; they tell CodeSOTA apart by "codesota.com, /api/sota, 'refreshed live'" and "codesota.com, routing layer, /api/sota", and the Papers with Code battery checks that CodeSOTA is not presented as Papers with Code.
